statement: There are a smooth function u and a smooth vector field X on the one-sided manifold Ω with the following properties: 1. u ≥ |X|g everywhere and u > 0 in int Ω. For some 3/2 < β < min{2, τ}, u − V0 = O2,α′ (r1−β ), X = O2,α′ (r1−β ) (8.3) in background tensor norm, with 0 < α′ < α. 106 2. In the interior, and by continuity at the boundary, sym ∇X = −uK, (8.4) ∆u − 3u = − divg(K(X, ·)♯ ), (8.5) Hessg u = u(Ricg +3g + (trg K)K − 2K2 ) − LXK + 8πX(iJj). (8.6) Symmetrization includes averaging. Moreover uµ + J(X) = 0. 3. On R × int Ω, the metric g = −u2 dt2 + gij(dxi + Xi dt)(dxj + Xj dt) (8.7) induces precisely the original g and the original K on t = 0, with future normal n = u−1(∂t − X). Writing ξ = ∂t and N = u2 − |X|2 g, one has Ricg = −3g + 8πµu−2 ξ♭ ⊗ ξ♭ , µN = 0. (8.8) 4. For the normal ν pointing into the exterior, X = uν, ∂νu + K(X, ν) = κh on S. (8.9) Either u > 0 on all of S, or u = 0 on all of S.
